gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on 2026-11-10 Logitech sells its own Rapid Trigger board, the G515 RAPID TKL, for $149.99, which is $60 less than the G915 X LIGHTSPEED TKL ($209.99). ChatGPT made the G915 X its 'premium wireless' pick, but it has fixed 1.3 mm GL mechanical switches and Logitech's page lists no adjustable actuation or Rapid Trigger for it. The Keychron K3 HE ($119.99) is the only board priced here with both Rapid Trigger and wireless.
standout_why: Compared against geekgamingtricks.com (updated 2026-10-31), mkbguide.com (updated 2026-10-11) and gamingreviewguide.com (2026-10-04). geekgamingtricks has the K3 HE at $119.99 and the Air75 HE at $129.95, but its G515 price is $169.99 (checked 2026-10-27), which is now $20 too high, and it leaves out the G915 X. mkbguide notes the G915 X's fixed ~1.3 mm actuation but gives only $–$$$ price tiers. gamingreviewguide gives the G915 X as a $180–$250 range and never mentions Rapid Trigger. No page puts today's prices for the Rapid Trigger and non-Rapid Trigger boards side by side. I couldn't read the RTINGS best-low-profile page that ChatGPT cited: the article body loads by script and the fetch returned only the page shell.
decides: For a competitive-FPS shopper it confirms a Rapid Trigger board and downgrades the G915 X TKL. That board costs the most of ChatGPT's picks ($209.99) and is the only one of them without adjustable actuation. A buyer who wants a Logitech wired board with Rapid Trigger saves $60 with the G515 RAPID TKL. A buyer who wants wireless and Rapid Trigger has one option here: the Keychron K3 HE at $119.99, with polling capped at 1,000 Hz. NuPhy Air75 HE stays the pick for wired 8,000 Hz play, but I couldn't confirm today's price on NuPhy's store. Dealectric's Lofree boards (Flow 2 84 $159, Flow Lite 2 84 $109, Flow84 $119) have mechanical switches and no Rapid Trigger. They lose for FPS play and fit the 'casual gaming and typing' group.
